result.description: Web hosting and deployment platform: atomic deploys, serverless functions, forms, DNS, and more.
result.auth_detail: Personal access token (generated in user settings) sent as Authorization: Bearer header for single-account use. OAuth2 authorization-code (app client key and secret, registered in user settings) required for public integrations.
result.access_detail: A Free plan exists at $0. Anyone can sign up, generate a PAT, or register an OAuth app in user settings with no review. Docs say OAuth2 is required for public integrations, but OAuth app registration is self-serve. Free plan has a 300 credit limit.
result.api_notes: REST API at https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/ with a public OpenAPI spec at open-api.netlify.com. Covers sites, deploys, forms, DNS, snippets, and more. Go and JS clients generated from the spec.

evidence.quote: To authenticate API requests, include the token in the authorization header:
If you’re making a public integration with Netlify for others to enjoy, you must use OAuth2.
You can register a new application in your Netlify user settings for OAuth applications.
Use the Netlify REST API to manage atomic deploys of your sites and apps, manage form submissions, inject JavaScript snippets, manage DNS, and so much more.
Netlify offers an MCP server, which you can connect to through a connector, plugin, or your agent.
